findings.title: Chained: reflected XSS + session cookie without HttpOnly -> session hijacking
findings.description: The verified reflected-XSS sink executes attacker-controlled JavaScript in a victim's browser, and the application's session cookie(s) (SESSIONID, jwt_session) are readable from JavaScript because they lack the HttpOnly attribute. An attacker only needs the XSS to run once to copy the session cookie and take over the victim session -- no credential access required.
findings.evidence: 1) XSS: The scanner confirmed that executable JavaScript payloads (, , ) are reflected into the response with no encoding or filtering -- a browser will execute them in the victim's session. This upgrades the finding from 'reflected markup' to a working cross-site scripting exploit. 2) session cookies visible to JavaScript: SESSIONID, jwt_session (no HttpOnly flag observed on the Set-Cookie headers captured this session)
findings.remediation: Set HttpOnly (and Secure) on every session cookie; add a Content-Security-Policy that blocks inline script; fix the XSS sink.
